findings.text: When a class defines its own __rich_repr__ method and uses @auto(angular=True), the angular attribute is never set on the existing method (line 119-122 only sets it if __rich_repr__ doesn't exist). This causes auto_repr at line 66 to always get angular=False via getattr's default, producing non-angular output like 'Foo(...)' instead of '<Foo ...>' even when angular=True was requested.

0.reason: The angular attribute is only set inside the `if not hasattr(cls, "__rich_repr__")` block, so when a class already defines `__rich_repr__` and uses `@auto(angular=True)`, the angular flag is never applied and `auto_repr` reads `angular=False`.
